# _…on a new wave of support_ Copper, the bell weather of global economic activity, has raced ahead in recen

t weeks with prices up 9% since the end of August. As the threat of a double dip recession has diminished in the USA and Europe, positive leading indicators emanate from Asia, and China in particular, pointing to a far more bullish story for the red metal than most analysts anticipated at the start of this year. Despite a mixture of both positive and negative economic news feeds since March, there has not been one disappointing story or data point on copper demand. It is **6200 RHS (inverted)** still very much an Asian centric recovery but there are **6000Jan-10 Feb-10 Mar-10 Apr-10 May-10 Jun-10 Jul-10 Aug-10 Sep-10** some small positives from the US and Europe (mainly but Data: LME, US Federal Reserve not exclusively Northern Europe) in both the wirerod and brass mill sectors. There has been steady growth throughout the year with sheet and strip demand for electronics, automotive and semiconductors all still white hot globally. Three-month copper prices have scaled higher since hitting a low of $6,050/t in early June, to breach $7,000/t by the end of July and threatening $7,500/t by the end of August. As sentiment turned even more bullish recently it was not surprising that the three-month LME copper price tipped highs of $8,027/t by the end of last week, 24th September. Some producer selling and general profit taking pushed prices lower to close at $7,945/t, while the cash to three month spread also slipped into a backwardation of $1/t versus a contango of $9/t on that trading day(Friday 24th September). Bullish macro and fundamental news have pushed prices for the red metal north again and on Wednesday 29th September prices had again broken through the $8,000/t barrier, gaining significant momentum from the latest positive Chinese macro indicator. The HSBC China Purchasing Managers' Index rose to a five-month high in September and registered a second consecutive monthly increase. This emphasises our view that following a softer summer demand in China is strengthening again. Some dollar softness and the news that Sterlite Industries has received a court directive to shutter its 400,000t Tuticorin smelter added further fuel to drive prices through the psychologically important $8,000/t level. Indeed even prior t

o this latest piece of supply news, which we estimate will curb output by around 80,000t in Q4, we had seen the surpluses eroded as global refined consumption growth (8.4%) continued to outpace that of production (1.1 %) and exchange stocks were trimmed. This comes despite a retracement on SHFE which saw 3-month prices fall to lows of RMB57,280/t following an unanticipated announcement from the Chinese government of further controls on the property market. Under the policy, banks will now have to demand a down payment of at least 30% from all mortgage applicants as part of the governments bid to cap property prices. Copper prices on SHFE have since recovered and closed higher at RMB60,600/t, recovering its losses given the policy is neutral to metals in the short term. Overall, market sentiment remains subdued on the SHFE, not just in response to this latest government policy announcement but also ahead of the Chinese National Holiday (1st-7th October) that begins tomorrow. SHFE 3-month prices failed to match the pace of the increase on the LME when markets re-opened on 27th September after the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival. Even though expectations are for further strength in LME prices over the coming weeks, Chinese participants do not expect SHFE prices to track the pace of LME increases when the Chinese market re-opens after the extended break. #### _Abnormal stock declines compared to Q3 norm Monthly LME stock change, 1970-2010_ ‘000 tonnes

#### _Stocks support_ Inventories across the exchanges have been steadily drawn 20 down over the past month. On the LME in particular, inventories have declined consecutively over the past three 10 months when traditionally they build during the seasonally - slower summer months for demand in the Northern -10 hemisphere. Currently, stocks on the LME are at levels of -20 374,150 tonnes last seen in November 2009 and 32% off the -30 555,075 tonne high registered in mid-February. Not since 2000 have stocks been drawn down in each month during the -40 Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct third quarter. Indeed there have only been four years, 1978

, Data: LME, CRU Analysis 1979, 1984 and 2000, when stocks have been drawn down in each month during the period. Inventories on Comex are also down, close to November 2009 levels of around 77,000 tonnes. Reported stocks in China are also dwindling, down by 6,918 tonnes this week to 87,447 tonnes. This is the lowest level of SHFE copper stocks for a year and stocks are now some 100,000 tonnes or 50% below the late April high of 189,441 tonnes. #### _Premium mating season looms_ When China does re-open, LME week will be almost upon us and producers and consumers will once again begin their courtship over the annual premium. This time last year there was no clarity as to the prospects for demand and negotiations proved difficult. Producers were concerned that consumers would be reluctant to accept the terms on offer and contract negotiations were extended into early 2010, with European benchmark premiums agreed at around $80/t. Debate amongst market participants is already in full swing ahead of these meetings, with the consensus that the producers will try to push through higher premiums for 2011. The erosion of the surplus through © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 16 October 2010 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com Reported Chilean tenders dry up

2010 coupled with a rising trend in spot premia in Europe and the USA over this last quarter supports expectations for higher terms across all regions next year. In addition, the promising supply/demand picture for 2011 implies that the market should be able to bear higher levels, with some suggesting a return to a 3-figure benchmark for European contracts. Spot premia remain unchanged on the levels quoted last month, a reflection of limited business given that most 80 consumers are covered for the remainder of the year, but 60 also that there is not much available to sell. In Europe, spot premiums have been supported in a $80-100/t range on a 40 CIF Rotterdam basis while in the USA they are being 20 quoted in a broad range of 5-6.5¢/lb. We also understand Chinese buyers are increasingly looking to source higher grades of scrap. Meanwhile, the spot premium in China for imported copper cathodes has edged higher since last month to $80-120/t. There has been only one Chilean tender confirmed from Pucobre for non-LME registered cathode for 1,800t (600t/m October to December 2010) at a premium of $90/t with a M+1 QP. There have been few reported tenders from the Chilean producers. Views vary from “producers have no additional material for sale” to “producers are h

olding off material to support premiums higher ahead of the annual negotiations”. We believe that producers have had limited material for sale this year. Material, when available has been sold following private negotiation rather than on the open market. #### _Troubles ahead?_ 2010 has been remarkable in that disruptions through the supply chain have been minimal, outside of the latest development at Tuticorin in India. Yet supply has still fallen short of demand requirements and the threat of further disruption is very much at the forefront. Codelco’s labour issues (both contract negotiations at its Divisions and its retirement policy) could still erupt and lead to further supply outages this year. Labour contract negotiations at Collahuasi could also add to the overall raw material constraint already in place. These constraints have also affected consumers. As demand has increased this year, supported by restocking through the downstream consumption chain and a recovery in end-use demand, we understand that some brass mills (particularly those in Asia) have had to source cathode in the absence of readily available scrap. Moreover, the news feeds about copper theft rising in tandem with the value of the red metal, further support our view that this market is still very tight. Across the globe, from large cities such as San Francisco to small villages in the UK, cases of copper theft (from cell phone towers and power substations) are on the increase. These incidents also support our theory that there is very little easily accessible and available scrap and that the scrap pool that had been in existence several years ago has been totally whittled away. In the current market, any scrap that does come through is quickly bought and consumed or held in anticipation of higher prices and a greater profit. The shortfall in the concentrates market remains engrained, leading to announcements of cut backs at some producers (PPC and Mitsubishi). With few projects in the pipeline to boost production next year and scrap availability tight, only a sharp slump in consumption next year would lead to a balance refined market, given our current production estimates. All of the above leads us to believe the short term bias to prices will be on the high side. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 16 October 2010 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com |_Exchange statistics_|_, price_

## **Copper plate, sheet and strip** 

According to our estimates, world copper PSS production rose by 31% y-o-y to 552,000t in Q2 2010. Production growth in Asia outperformed that in the rest of the world.  Chinese output registered an increase of 43% y-o-y to 193,000t in Q2.  That was also up by 17% from Q1 2010.  The North East Asian region registered 41% y-o-y growth in output to 154,000t.  However, from a sequential point of view the figure was flat due to stable local and foreign demand.  European output totalled 134,000t in Q2 2010, a 24% increase from year-ago levels.  It was also up by 23% sequentially supported by strong consumption in Germany, and Eastern and Central Europe.  In addition, Germany experienced strong sequential growth in its exports.  US output exhibited some promising rebound signs in Q2 2010.  Production amounted to 30,000t, a 26% increase from the same period in 2009.  It was also up by 16% from the previous quarter, attributed to a rebound in domestic consumption. 

## **Copper alloy plate, sheet and strip** 

World copper alloy PSS output amounted to 564,000t in Q2 2010, an increase of 33% y-o-y.  Production levels were up sequentially by 8%.  Chinese output advanced by 24% y-o-y to 201,000t, supported by significant capacity additions in recent years.  North East Asian output surged by 50% y-o-y to 104,000t, reaching again levels seen before the global economic crisis.  Production in Q2 was up by 8% from the previous quarter.  Boosted by a recovery in domestic consumption, which more than doubled to 29,000t in Q2, Japanese output surged by 80% y-o-y to 45,000t.  This domestic demand growth was also backed by strong exports.  South Korean output totalled 40,000t in Q2 whilst that of Taiwan 19,000t.  In both cases, output exceeded levels before the crisis attributed to robust growth in end-use markets.  European output was 118,000t in Q2, up 52% y-o-y and 11% q-o-q.  Germany’s estimated output was 55,000t, fuelled by a very strong rebound in exports to 45,000t and robust domestic consumption that reached 20,000t, levels close to those before the crisis.  US production was 65,000t in Q2, up by 35% y-o-y but down by 3% q-o-q.  The US production growth experienced in Q1 was largely a result of restocking; with such rates being unsustainable in the longer term as consumption is unlikely to exceed previous highs. 

## **Tales from the marketplace – Asia-centric growth boosts output** 

Market evidence shows that copper and alloy flat rolled products continued to outperform other copper semis, supported by robust demand from the digital appliance, semiconductor and automotive industries. An undisclosed Chinese plate and strip fabricator reported that the Anhui-based company has a full order book for the rest of the year.  Thin copper strip used in electronics has seen the strongest growth.  CRU expects that demand from the Chinese automotive sector will remain strong, partly backed by a pilot programme in five c

ities that provides subsidies to manufacturers of electric and hybrid cars.  Japanese output of flat rolled products exhibited steady recovery, benefiting from government subsidies for environmentally friendly cars and strong exports to China and other Asian countries.  Japanese sheet and strip fabricators were running at full capacity to meet demand for semiconductor leadframes and automotive connector pins, significantly improving profitability since these are high-value added products.  CRU anticipates that the end of subsidies for eco-friendly cars at the end of September, coupled with a strong yen will challenge the Japanese flat rolled products industry in Q4 2010.  Italy’s **KME** reported that it saw improved demand for its rolled products from the automotive, industrial and domestic appliance sectors.  Its best performing market was Germany, driven by strong foreign demand for end-use products such as premium brand vehicles exported to China.

## **Continuing recovery in wire and cable demand driving wirerod production** 

In all the major markets around the world copper wire and cable production has grown this year compared to the same period in 2009, and as a result production of copper wirerod has been increasing.  At a global level we estimate that copper wirerod production in the period Q1-Q3 2010 grew by 6.5% y-o-y. Growth has been relatively stable throughout this year so far with q-o-q increases of around 6-7% in each of the first three quarters.  The main growth driver has been the winding wire sector, where a rebound in the production of electrical equipment coupled with the strength in the automotive sector and the growth in production of electric vehicles has led to a 14.9% rise in consumption in the first three quarters of this year.  However, despite this strong rebound, winding wire production is still below the previous peak seen in Q1-Q3 2007.  The winding wire sector is a good indicator of how the fortunes of the rest of the cable industry will be as it is a leading indicator of the health of the whole wire and cable sector.  Demand for cables associated with construction projects, such as building wire and power cable, will typically lag and so growth here is much more muted this year.  In many parts of the world, particularly in Europe and North America, it will be well into 2011 at the earliest before demand from this sector begins to show any strong recovery. 

## **Asia remains the main driver** 

Copper wirerod demand continues to be healthy in South America, particularly Brazil, and North Africa, but it is Asia that continues to be the principal engine of growth.  Even before the current global recession struck, Asia’s share of the global wire and cable market had been rising and this crisis has only accelerated this trend.  In the first three quarters of 2007 Asia accounted for 52% of total global

copper wirerod consumption. By the same period in 2010 this had risen to just under 62%. Demand in China continues to grow strongly and the Indian market is also strong. In the Gulf region demand is continuing to rise, despite the weakness of the Dubai market, with significant further potential in other parts of the UAE, plus Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait. ## **Wire and cable demand outlook is very positive** Historically copper wire and cable production and hence demand for copper wirerod grew at a similar rate to global GDP at around 3%. Then in the middle of the last decade it started to outperform GDP, primarily driven by China, the Middle East and other developing countries. As a country develops it will typically consume large quantities of wire and cable as it builds out its infrastructure and then as the economy matures growth in consumption of wire and cable will slow. As the economy becomes more mature and population growth slows and manufacturing industries move offshore consumption can then start to fall. This cycle will continue, but on top of it is a new factor which is the move to renewable energy generation and a reduction in the use of hydrocarbons as a source of energy. It has been said that the last century was the era of fossil fuels, but that this is now ending and we are entering the era of electricity. As we move forward, electricity will more and more become the main source of energy and this has implications for demand for wire and cable. In the developed world electricity transmission and distribution grids evolved to transmit power from large generation stations located relatively close to the centres of consumption. Now, though, renewable energy generation and the development of smart grids means that this model is no longer ideal and so grids will need to be re-engineered. This will inevitably involve significant volumes of wire and cable. Whilst we envisage that the substitution of aluminium for copper in power cables will rise, demand for copper wirerod in wire and cable is still expected to increase at above historical trend rates in the face of this global electrification process. © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 10 of 16 October 2010 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com |_Copper plat_|_e, s_|_heet,_|_strip_|_and_|_foil_||||||||||| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |**('000 tonnes)**|||**2008**|||**% Ch**|||**2009**|||**% Ch**|**20**|**10**|**% Ch**| ||**Q1**|**Q2**|**Q3**

# _Industry News_ ## **Mine Production** - On 27th August, **First Quantum Minerals** (FQM) announced the suspension of operations at its **Frontier** mine in the DR Congo. The suspension followed the withdrawal of FQM’s exploitation permit by the DR Congo’s mining registry CAMI, and word received from the state miner SODIMICO stating that it has been awarded the titles to the Frontier concession. SODIMICO has demanded that FQM cease its activities and

vacate the land. FQM stated that the withdrawal of the mining licence is against DR Congo law and added that it will bring this latest incident concerning the loss of Frontier to international arbitration along with the **Kolwezi Project** and will pursue all other legal avenues available.  Prior to this, Frontier was expected to produce 80,000t of copper-inconcentrate in 2010, but this has been reduced to 60,000t in light of the above. 

- Reports in early September suggest that **Codelco** is looking to shed up to 3,000 staff by the year-end by offering up to 15% of its workforce retirement.  The company plans to restructure staff and management to increase productivity and enable it to better compete with leaner private sector rivals. At the same time, Codelco also plans to hire new personnel.  The new CEO, Diego Hernandez, has already reorganised the company's mining divisions, scrapping two existing vice-presidencies while

- **Codelco’s** management presented, at the beginning of September, an early proposal for a new collective labour contract to the unionised workers at **Radomiro Tomic** (part of the **Codelco Norte Division** ), as the current contract is due to expire in November 2010.  However, unionised workers voted to reject the proposal on Wednesday 15<sup>th</sup> September.  Meanwhile, Codelco offered an early retirement scheme to workers at the **El Teniente Division** .  In this case, it was reported that a number of workers accepted the proposal and will each receive around US$160,000.  In addition, workers at Codelco Norte are scheduled to start negotiations for early retirement by the end of September.  In 2010, CRU expects Codelco to produce 1,700,000t of contained copper. 

- On 20<sup>th</sup> September, it was reported that the **Zambian government** announced that it is negotiating higher power rates with foreign mining companies.  Rates will increase to “cost-reflective” levels by 2013 and the increases are to contribute to investment in new power generation facilities, which would include increasing the national generation capacity from 1,400MW to 1,800MW as well as improving the distribution system. 

## **Exploration and Development** 







- On 15<sup>th</sup> September, **First Quantum Minerals** (FQM) announced that it had begun legal proceedings against subsidiaries of **ENRC** in a court in the British Virgin Islands; “as part of [FQM’s] efforts to pursue its rights in relation to the unlawful expropriation of its legal title to the **Kolwezi Project** .” FQM spent $750M on the project until the government of DR Co

ngo stripped the company’s rights to the concession in September 2009 following a national review of mining operations.  In August 2010, ENRC acquired a 50.5% stake in **Camrose Resources** , giving the multi-metal miner a majority stake in the project. 

- On 17<sup>th</sup> September, **Continental Minerals** (Canada) announced it has signed a letter of agreement with **Jinchuan Group** (China) to be acquired by them.  Jinchuan has agreed to buy 100% of Continental’s shares for C$432M (~US$421M).  Continental Minerals is a junior company whose main asset is the **Xietongmen** copper-gold deposit in Tibet.  The project is under exploration and its reserves have been estimated at 182.1Mt @0.455%Cu, 0.62g/t Au and 4.04g/t Ag.  CRU envisages start up of this mine in 2013 at a rate of 53,000tpy of copper-in-concentrate. 

- **Antofagasta Minerals** announced on 24<sup>th</sup> September that there have been no changes to the development schedule of its **Antucoya** project in Chile.  This follows a Chilean press report on 23<sup>rd</sup> September quoting the company’s CEO as saying that it may delay the project if the government passes into law its proposed increases to mining royalties.  The project is currently undergoing a feasibility study with a decision on development due next year.  Antucoya is an oxide deposit with an average copper grade of 0.27%, according to the company’s website. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 



- On 29th September, the Madras high court in India ordered the closure of **Sterlite** ’s **Tuticorin** smelter due to environmental code violations. The judge ruled that air and ground water pollution has reached unacceptably high levels and is endangering conditions in the Gulf of Mannar National Marine Park, located less than 25km from the plant.  Sterlite’s parent company, **Vedanta** , later announced that it had shut the plant, and is awaiting the full text of the ruling to consider its next move.

- On 15<sup>th</sup> September, **Pan Pacific Copper** (PPC) announced a reduction in its projected production for the coming October-March period given the low terms that smelters are getting to process copper and a shortage of scrap materials.  According to the announcement, this will reduce production 13% below full capacity levels, which represents a further cutback as the company had been producing at a level of 7% below full capacity since January 2009.  In 2010, PPC was expected to produce 657,000t of copper blister.  The refined copper producer operates the **Saganoseki** and **Tamano** smelters/refineries, as well as the **Hitachi** refinery. 

- Following PPC’s announcement, **Mitsubishi** also announced that it would be reducing smelter production by 5-7% in the October-March period.  However, the cut will largely be due to maintenance closures at its two smelters.  The company operates the **

Onahama** and the **Naoshima** smelters.  The company will close the Onahama smelter for maintenance for 14 days in late October and shut the Naoshima smelter for 18 days in February 2011. 

- **Vale** announced that in the auction of the tender offer to acquire shares of **Paranapanema S.A.** that took place on 1<sup>st</sup> September, the number of Paranapanema S.A. shares tendered did not reach the minimum level requirement to which the offer was conditioned. As a result, Vale did not acquire any Paranapanema S.A. shares in the auction. Vale had previously announced their intention to buy up to 100% common shares of Paranapanema S.A., subject to the purchase of at least 50% plus one common shares.  Paranapanema, which is valued at R2B (~US$1.1B), owns the Caraiba Metais smelter and refinery. 

## **Consumption** 







- Japanese output of copper and copper alloy semis increased by 18.2% y-o-y in August to 65,820t, the 10th consecutive month of y-o-y increases, according to data released by the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** .  It was reported that industry has been supported by exports to emerging markets rather than domestic consumption. Output in August was down from July’s output of 75,860t.  The association has revised its FY 2010-2011 output forecast up to 865,400t from its March projection of 855,000t.  In addition, Japanese copper wire and cable shipments in August rose by 5.5% y-o-y to 53,300t - the eighth straight month of y-o-y gains - supported by solid demand from the automobile and electronics sectors.  However, deliveries were down by 10.5% from July, data from the **Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association** showed.  Construction sector shipments showed the first y-o-y increase in 23 months, up by 4.4%.  The association revised its FY 2010-2011 demand outlook up by 0.5% to 666,000t on expectations of rising exports to Asia. 

- US imports of brass mill products rose by 19.8% y-o-y to 43.2M lbs in July, while exports fell by 0.2% y-o-y to 18.6M lbs, according to data from the **Copper and Brass Fabricators Council** . Canada was the leading export destination in July (6.0M lbs) while Germany supplied the most imports (8.6M lbs).  Imports/exports breakdown was: sheet, strip, plate and foil products 13.0M lbs/ 7.9M lbs; pipe and tube products 16.7M lbs/ 4.5M lbs; rods, bars and sections 10.4M lbs/ 4.2M lbs; copper alloy wire 3.2M lbs/ 1.9M lbs. 

- August imports of copper and copper products by China, the world’s largest consumer, advanced for a second month in succession to 379,527t, according to data from the Chinese customs.  Volumes were up by 11% from 342,901t in July, and up by 17% from 325,098t in August last year, on expectations of an increase in demand and on delivery of orders placed by arbitrage traders during July when it was profitable to bring in metal.  China also imported 400,000t of copper scrap in August, up from 380,000t in July.

- Finland’s **Luvata** plans to bring a new 30,000 sq.ft. manufacturing facility online in the US by Q2 2011, in order to increase production of its **Sunwire** photovoltaic (PV) wire, which is a copper-based, tin alloy plated flat PV wire used to connect silicon cells and thin-film solar panels.  The company is negotiating to lease a site for the dedicated Sunwire facility in Appleton, WI, where it already operates two copper alloy wire manufacturing facilities. 

- **Elektrokoppar** of Sweden, Europe’s fifth largest copper wirerod producer, said that Europe’s demand for copper will rise by approximately 3% in H2 2010 from H1, driven by improved end-use consumption rather than restocking.  In addition, they anticipate that world copper demand will also rise by 2%.  The company saw strong demand for winding wire in spring 2010 and its order books looked reasonably good for September.  They expect that copper prices will remain above the US$7,000/t level for the rest of 2010. 

- **Delphi** , the wiring harness manufacturer, plans to shut down its Czech unit.  The plant is located at Ceska Lipa, 90 km north of Prague, and serves automotive makers such as **BMW** and **Audi** .  The job cuts will take place in stages until the closure will be completed by the end of May 2011.  As a result, all 1,400 employees will be affected.  The trade union commented that the company plans to relocate operations to lower cost locations.  The Czech Republic has attracted foreign investment related to the automotive industry, but due to rising costs some companies are now deciding to relocate. 

- The US **Department of Commerce** announced its decision to impose anti-dumping duties on copper pipes and tubes from China and Mexico.  This is the third out of four decisions needed to make the tariffs final, with the final ruling due on 8<sup>th</sup> November.  The duties are fixed at a range of 11.25%60.85% on US$233M of imports from China and 24.89%-31.43% on US$130M of imports from Mexico. **Zhejiang Hailiang Co.** , China’s largest publicly traded copper tube maker, had its preliminary duties of 58.69% raised to 60.85%; **Golden Dragon Precise Copper Tube Group Inc.** faces an 11.25% duty whilst other major Chinese fabricators will pay 36.05%.
